relevance_note: The paper describes one identifiable neonate with HA20 caused by a deletion including TNFAIP3 ("she was definitively diagnosed with HA20") and summarises 11 further published patients with 6q deletions including TNFAIP3 in Table 1.
method_note: Read the paper by hand (full text, Table 1, references); no script transcribed the table, but Table 1 was typed by hand and every table span is the contiguous row prefix from the row label up to that patient's column, so each span is verbatim. Scope: Table 1 shows 12 patients as columns. Header row 1 gives each patient's source publication (Current report, Endo et al., Franco-Jarava et al., Sun et al, Taniguchi et al., Tsuchida et al., Viel et al., Wan et al., Wu et al.), copied verbatim into source_reference_in_review; header row 2 gives the paper's own labels Patient 1 - Patient 12, used as individual_label_in_paper. Patient 1 is the neonate of this report (the single patient of the case report, is_proband true); Patients 2-12 are literature cases from references [13-20] and are not probands. No relatives are described, so there are no relative rows. Table 1's only legend is 'AIHA Autoimmune hemolytic anemia, HLH Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis'; it does not define '+' or '-', so per D-22 a '-' cell is not evidence of absence: '-' cells are left 'not reported' and produce no phenotypic_features rows. '+' cells are read as observed, which is an assumption, and the table's 'Not mentioned' cells are also not reported. 'AIHA' is read as the autoimmune cytopenia of the checklist and 'HLH' as a feature in its own right. Table 1's 'Initial symptoms' cells hold several values that were stacked on separate lines and are printed run together (e.g. 'FeverAIHA', 'FeverRespiratory- infectionsGastroenteritis', 'AllergyRosacea'); per D-31 they were not assigned to people by position, and each patient's whole cell is recorded verbatim as one feature. The only checklist items taken from those cells are ones printed word for word: 'Gastroenteritis' for Patient 4 (gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation) and 'Henoch-Schonlein purpura' for Patient 9 (vasculitis). Table 1's 'Size of deletion' row (5.15 Mb for Patient 1, 0.119-13.13 Mb for Patients 2-12) has no schema field and was not recorded. No variant description is printed for Patients 2-12 (their deletions appear only in Fig. 2, which is not available), so their variant_original_string is 'not reported' per D-22, with gene symbol TNFAIP3 and the printed group wording for the type. The paper calls the deletions 'pathogenic' only in general terms (Fig. 2 caption 'Schematic representation of pathogenic deletions in chromosome 6 affectingTNFAIP3'), which D-29 excludes, so pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors is 'not reported' for everyone. Zygosity is printed only for Patient 1 ('heterozygous'). Inheritance is taken from Table 1's 'Inheritance' row for each patient's own column: 'de novo' recorded as de novo, 'paternal' as inherited paternal, 'maternal' as inherited maternal, 'unknown' as not reported; the paper gives no parental testing, so parental_testing_statement is 'not reported' for all and the de novo entries rest on the table's own word. Normal findings were recorded as the abnormality they rule out ('Measurement of autoantibodies ... were normal' -> autoantibodies excluded); an examination as a whole (ophthalmologic assessment, hearing test, brain MRI, abdominal ultrasonography) is written as the paper does and excludes no specific checklist item, so uveitis/ocular inflammation and central nervous system involvement stay 'not reported'. Patient 1's liver findings are recorded as hepatomegaly, hepatic dysfunction, elevated liver enzymes and hepatic injury; 'autoimmune hepatitis' and 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' stay 'not reported' for her because the paper never calls her liver disease or anaemia autoimmune (her anaemia is 'acute severe', with haemolysis excluded). Points noted rather than treated as contradictions: Table 1 lists Patient 1's spleen as enlarged on admission while the text later says 'her spleen was not palpable' (a change over time, so both phenotypic_features rows are kept); the Results say 'only 11 patients with HA20 molecularly confirmed to be caused by deletion of chromosome 6q have been reported since 2016' while Table 1 and the Discussion count 12 in total (11 previously reported plus this neonate); the text says 'eigtht were female' while Table 1 lists nine females; Table 1 gives Patients 2 and 3 'AIHA' as initial symptom while their 'Fever' cell is negative. Group counts without names ('eigtht were female', 'five presented with de novo deletions', 'Nine patients experienced early-onset symptoms', 'in seven patients, the initial symptoms were unprovoked and recurrent episodes of fever') were used to exclude nobody. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false: the earlier patients come from other publications (references [13-20]) and the paper never says its own patient was described before.
